question_text: Cassie made an initial investment of €2000 into a savings account, and followed it with regular deposits of €500 per quarter. The account pays $1.2\%$ interest per quarter, and inflation is $0.3\%$ per quarter.

subparts.stem: Explain why the real interest rate is approximately $0.9\%$ per quarter.

mark_breakdown.desc: Using the relationship: real interest multiplier $\times$ inflation multiplier = nominal interest multiplier

subparts.solution:
$\text{real interest rate multiplier} \times 1.003 = 1.012$
$\therefore \text{real interest rate multiplier} = \frac{1.012}{1.003} \approx 1.00897$
$\therefore \text{real interest rate} \approx 0.897\% \approx 0.9\%$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Fisher equation in multiplier form: $(1 + r_r)(1 + i) = (1 + r_n)$, where $r_r$ is the real rate, $i$ is inflation, and $r_n$ is the nominal rate.
step_by_step: Identify nominal multiplier $1 + 0.012 = 1.012$ and inflation multiplier $1 + 0.003 = 1.003$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Simply subtracting inflation from the nominal rate ($1.2\% - 0.3\% = 0.9\%$) without showing the exact multiplicative relationship when required.

subparts.stem: Find the real value of Cassie's investment after 5 years.

mark_breakdown.desc: Using TVM solver to find future value in savings account after 5 years

subparts.solution:
$N = 5 \times 4 = 20$, $I\% = 1.2$, $PV = -2000$, $\text{PMT} = -500$, $P/Y = 4$, $C/Y = 4$
$\therefore FV \approx 12\,413.68$
After 5 years, Cassie will have €$12\,413.68$ in her savings account.
Now $\text{real value} \times (1.003)^{5 \times 4} = €12\,413.68$
$\therefore \text{real value} = \frac{€12\,413.68}{(1.003)^{20}} \approx €11\,691.81$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The real value of a future sum of money is obtained by deflating the nominal value by the inflation factor $(1 + i)^N$.
step_by_step: Calculate nominal future value using TVM: $N = 20$, $I\% = 1.2$, $PV = -2000$, $\text{PMT} = -500$, giving $FV \approx 12413.68$.
Identify the quarterly inflation rate of $0.3\%$, corresponding to multiplier $1.003$ per quarter.
Over 20 quarters, total inflation factor is $(1.003)^{20}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Applying the annual inflation adjustment instead of compounding it per quarter for 20 quarters.
